tickets.title: Decide: test the playground in Firefox and Safari (and in CI), or document Chrome-only as final
tickets.body:
`web/test.sh` (docs/testing.md, "Browser tests") runs the playground tests in headless Chrome only, locally; they are not in `nix flake check` because Chrome isn't in the Nix build sandbox and one test waits out the real 15 s timeout. Firefox and Safari are untested. The goal is a public static site (see the playground notes), so other browsers will be used.

First step: decide (a) a manual cross-browser checklist run before a public release, (b) Firefox via WebDriver BiDi/Playwright in the same script, (c) leave as is. Safari can only be tested on a Mac.

Done when: the decision is recorded in docs/testing.md, plus the script/checklist if (a) or (b).

tickets.title: WebAssembly stack guard: measure limits in all browsers (incl. compact text) and choose the guard size
tickets.body:
Problem: each call uses stack in linear memory (which the guard measures) and the engine's own call stack (about 1 MiB in V8); the engine's runs out first, so the guard is 256 KiB (crates/web/build.rs, WASM_GUARD; override STITCHWORT_GUARD; it was 128 KiB until games/rogue's 11-field `State` was bundled), calibrated in Node and Chrome only. Firefox and Safari are unmeasured. 256 KiB gives about 25 levels of nesting and list literals of about 200 elements, with a margin of 2 only in Node/Chrome. The parser's stack use per level could also be cut (e.g. boxing `Diagnostic` in its `Result`): that is SW-126.

Change, one campaign: measure in all four engines with web/stress.html: nesting depth, long list/text literals (including compact `List Char` literals, d4d3626, which were only measured natively: the limit before E-RESOURCE and the time), then pick the guard size.

Eliminating recursion (stack-safe-evaluation steps 3 and 4, docs/proposals/stack-safe-evaluation.md) is the real fix; see also SW-62 (long literals) and SW-57 (JS limits in browsers, different subject: generated code).

Done when: a table of limits per browser (nesting, literal length, compact text) is in docs/evaluator-speed.md or compact-text.md and the guard is set from it.

History: split 19 Oct into SW-126; merged SW-61 (guard size) and SW-52 (compact text in WASM).

tickets.title: File-private declarations: `private def` visible only in its own file (helpers)
tickets.body:
Problem: helpers (AoC's twice*/window* lemmas, the prelude's Text.splitCons/splitChars) join their namespace; only their own file should see them (Matt, 20 Oct 2026). There's no `private` today: docs/proposals/multi-file.md:498 ('Visibility of declarations: everything'), :1390 (later list), namespaces.md §8 table.

First step: a short design note (docs/proposals/), with the sketch: `private` before def/theorem/type; the name resolves only in its file; two files of one namespace may each have a private `helper` (the full name gets a file-unique part, as Lean does); bodies stay visible to the checker so a public function using a private helper still unfolds in other files' proofs (hides the name, not the definition; unlike Idris `export`); naming it from another file is E-PRIVATE 'private to file X'. Precedents: Lean private, Agda private blocks, Rust, Scala/TS. Design review gate applies.

Done when: the note is reviewed, then `private` is built with accept/reject examples (including the same private name in two files) and the AoC/prelude helpers are marked.

History: Matt, 20 Oct 2026.

tickets.title: Partial callbacks inside List.map run on native, --js and the reference runner, stack-safe
tickets.body:
The problem: A function marked {Partial} (it might run forever) can only be called from other partial code. `List.map` with a partial callback is not yet supported by the runners (native, `--js`, the reference evaluator), so a partial function cannot be mapped over a list. This is lane 3b of docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md (section 7.4).

The change: make the three runners execute partial callbacks inside `map`, without growing the stack, and counting ticks exactly as the note specifies. The 4e generator gets partial callbacks through `map`.

What it should do: tick counts and traces agree across the runners; the 1M-element speed figures from the note are met; the `partial.rs` tick tests, `run_js`/`run_reference` on the new example and `effect_runtime` pass. Sonnet. Depends on 3a (library and elaborator part) being merged first.

tickets.title: Make calls to partial functions cheaper in the runners (about 3x slower than ordinary calls today)
tickets.body:
The problem: calls to {Partial} functions are about 3x slower than ordinary ones natively and about 2x in JS; half of the native cost is the request node a partial call builds (D1182, docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md section 5.4).

The change: runner fast paths plus a cheaper request node for partial calls, in both backends (D1182 A+B, lane 3d of the note, section 7.4).

What it should do: keep the change only if it gives at least 1.5x on `p2-collatz` (or the note's model comparison in `partial.rs`) with identical tick traces (D1219). If the gain is smaller, drop it and record the measurement on this ticket. Sonnet.

tickets.title: Run a partial function's tail self-calls as a loop
tickets.body:
The problem: a partial function that calls itself in tail position still builds a request and a frame per call (D1182 C, lane 3e of docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md).

The change: compile tail self-calls of partial functions to a direct loop in the runners, after SW-469.

What it should do: at least 1.5x faster on the loop shapes in the note (4e loop shapes, `p2-collatz`) with identical tick counts (D1219); otherwise drop it. Sonnet.

tickets.title: Constructor names: should they live inside their type (Quit vs GaveUp ambiguity), or be resolved by expected type?
tickets.body:
The problem: constructors of different union types share one namespace, so two types cannot both have a constructor `Quit`. The roguelike renamed its `Quit` to `GaveUp` for this reason (D2, NOTES stage 1 #8; unchecked wording).

The change: a design discussion with Matt first. Options: constructors nested in their type (`Outcome.Quit`), or resolving a bare name by the expected type, or leaving as is and documenting the rename trick.

What it should do: Matt picks one; if the answer is not "leave as is", a design note in docs/proposals/ follows. Label it `decision` so it shows up.

Raised by SW-3339: a lexer and a printer in one program (token Str vs layout Str) make | Str t => ambiguous even where the match's type is known; the toy formatter will hit it.

Opus paper started 12:00, expected 1.5 h: design note docs/proposals/constructor-names.md ahead of the full formatter.

12:10 review: docs/proposals/constructor-names.md written (not committed). Probed today: bare clashing constructors are E-AMBIGUOUS in patterns, values, arguments, lists, record updates and comparisons even with the type known; a file's own `None` breaks `| None` on an Option. Options (a) expected type first, (a') type as tie-break, (b) `.Ctor` only, (c) both, (d) status quo. Recommends (a): the known type's constructor wins, ambiguous names wait on the queue when the type isn't known yet; terms and hashes unchanged. Four stages, ~8-9 h (Sonnet 1.5 h, Opus 2 h, Opus 2-3 h, Sonnet 1.5 h). Question: D3615 (adopt (a)? rec yes).


D3615 (Matt, 15 Nov 2026): "option one plus a discipline to avoid files that need to import multiple clashing names unless it's code that genuinely must use both. The code organization habit. We can maybe think about going back to this dot shorthand as Lean does in three in the future, potentially. But yeah, for now, let's proceed with your suggestion." Not type-directed resolution (Matt: one name, one meaning per file, readable at a glance). Built as SW-3397; .C shorthand parked as SW-3398.

tickets.title: Terminal.simulate: make the frame accumulator visible so proofs can do induction over turns
tickets.body:
The problem: the roguelike proofs (PROOFS.md) cannot induct over the turns of a terminal run because `Terminal.simulate` hides its accumulated frames.

The change: expose the frame accumulator (a loop function with the accumulator as an argument and a lemma relating it to `simulate`), as the roguelike proof needs.

What it should do: a theorem about the whole run can be proved by induction over the turn list.

D1376 (26 Oct): left on backlog by Matt

tickets.title: Effect.bindAssoc's proof uses Quot.sound: can it avoid it?
tickets.body:
The problem: `Effect.bindAssoc` (associativity of bind) is assumed as an axiom in std. Every theorem that uses it shows up in `stitchwort audit` with an axiom, and the roguelike had to restructure its code (draw first, then plan) to avoid needing a proved monad law under handlers (rogue PROOFS.md gap 2).

The change: prove it (probably needs a computation-equality/extensionality principle for Comp), or restrict it to the handler-free case.

What it should do: no axiom left in std for the effect monad laws; `audit` clean on the roguelike generation theorems. Related: SW-570 (symbolic stepping through handlers), SW-660.

Board audit (5 Nov 2026): Effect.bindAssoc is a proved theorem since SW-405; what remains is only its use of Quot.sound.

tickets.title: An unannotated lambda inside an {IO} body makes List.map/fold run at {IO} instead of pure
tickets.body:
The problem: in a `main : {IO} ...` body, a lambda without a type annotation passed to an effect-polymorphic List function (map, foldLeft) is given the {IO} row, not the empty row, so a pure fold in main pays effect dispatch (the interpreter builds effect nodes it does not need).

The change: when the lambda body performs no effects, infer the empty row for the lambda (docs/proposals/effect-polymorphic-list.md covers the design; unchecked whether this is already on its roadmap).

What it should do: a pure inline fold inside main costs the same as outside it; a test in the bench or a step-count example shows no effect dispatch. "For Matt": asks for his go-ahead on the inference rule.

tickets.title: Effect runtime option B: run state-handler loops at an open effect row (design note and soundness argument)
tickets.body:
The problem: the effect runtime handles a state loop by capturing a resumption per operation. Option B in docs/proposals/effect-runtime.md section 9.11 (D1291) runs such loops directly when the handler's row is open.

The change: write the design note with a soundness argument and a measured cost model; no code until Matt agrees. Related: SW-593 (effect representation change, D1297 trigger met) and SW-1087 (report on handler fast paths).

What it should do: Matt decides D1291 from the note.

tickets.title: Compile IO directly in native binaries instead of going through the Rust IO runner (revisit D1298)
tickets.body:
The problem: native executables keep a Rust runner for IO (print/read), so every IO operation builds a Delay value and goes through the runner. D1298 kept it; Matt asked on 26 Oct to revisit.

The change: first measure the runner's share on an IO-heavy program (docs/proposals/native-only.md section 2). If large, generate code that calls the OS directly.

What it should do: a measured number on this ticket; then Matt decides. Related: SW-593.

tickets.title: Proofs about effectful code run out of resources stepping through handlers symbolically (E-RESOURCE)
tickets.body:
The problem: when a theorem is about code that runs under a handler (for example the roguelike generator under `seeded`), the checker steps through the handler symbolically and hits E-RESOURCE. The roguelike therefore uses one `next()` per turn and derives every roll from an index hash (the "Dice" workaround, SW-571 text below), so its invariants are proved on the pure `resolve` function only.

The change: find out what the checker needs so effectful code can be proved as written (rogue PROOFS.md "Tried" section lists the attempts). Candidate pieces: Effect.bindAssoc without an axiom (SW-548), a lemma "seeded equals list handler", cheaper symbolic stepping.

What it should do: the generation theorems (generatedReachable, generatedFramed, newGameSound, drawn*) are proved over the free-style {Random} generator, and the roguelike goes back to calling `roll` freely, deleting the index-hashing.

Merged in from SW-564 (backlog review, 4 Nov 2026): prove those generation theorems over the free-style generator; blocked by symbolic handler stepping (E-RESOURCE) and the Effect.bindAssoc axiom (PROOFS.md gaps #2-3). Matt asked to revisit, 26 Oct.
Merged in from SW-571 (backlog review, 4 Nov 2026): per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: `step` calls `next()` once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) ..., Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling `roll` freely. Then `seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c` by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants are proved about pure `resolve` for every seed. Revert to free `roll` once provable (D1305, Matt 26 Oct). Idea, untested: state invariants for any answers to `roll`, not via `seeded`.

tickets.title: run --native refuses to start under Linux strict overcommit (mode 2): it reserves 64 GiB on the CLI thread
tickets.body:
The problem: with vm.overcommit_memory=2, `stitchwort run --native` reserves its full 64 GiB up front on the CLI thread and the OS refuses.

The change: size the reservation before the thread starts. That needs the JIT code and the terminal to be movable across threads (open item from NO6/NO7).

What it should do: `run --native` starts under mode 2 on a machine with ordinary memory, reserving only what the program needs, or giving a clear error naming the limit.

tickets.title: cases follow-ups from a real program (26 Oct): (1) cases in t can't use a case's own split equations to fill t's holes, and those equations can't be named (E-UNSOLVED) — blocks Option-chain inversions; (2) hypotheses that are functions (∀ y, lookup = Some y → …) aren't applied, search runs into the 64-case budget; (3) splits goal atoms before following the hypothesis chain, descending into Float internals (820 ms then budget); (4) an unfolded Bool test is split as two independent atoms with impossible combinations left open; (5) decEq x x = No not treated as a contradiction; (6) one t must serve every case — a rewrite that finds nothing is an error where rfl would do; (7) cases as a bare function argument needs brackets
Signature defaults, stage 2: exported functions with defaults take a JS options object
tickets.body:
The problem: functions with default arguments (docs/proposals/signature-defaults.md) are exported to JavaScript with positional parameters, so a JS caller cannot omit defaults or name arguments.

The change: generate an options-object entry point for exported defaults (D1355).

What it should do: from JS, `f({ x: 1 })` works with the declared defaults, positional calls still work, and the generated TypeScript types show the optional fields.

tickets.title: Signature defaults, stage 3: constructor calls use field defaults
tickets.body:
The problem: fields can't have default values at construction: every constructor call must write every field.

The change: constructor calls use the defaults declared on the fields (D1346, docs/proposals/signature-defaults.md stage 3).

What it should do: `T (a := 1)` fills missing fields from their declared defaults, the same rules as functions, and hashes of existing code don't change.

Rename the always-true proposition Unit to something else (Truth/Top) and give the data unit type the name Unit
tickets.body:
The problem: `Unit` is a proposition (type Unit: Prop = | Trivial, core/Logic.sw:12), which misleads readers from Scala/Kotlin where Unit is the data type with one value. The data unit type has no name, only `()` (Builtin.UnitType, core/Effect.sw:94). `True` is taken by Bool's constructor. About 113 uses in std + examples (D1367, to consider).

The change: rename the proposition to `Truth` (proof `Trivial`); alternatives `Top` or the symbol `⊤`. Name the data type `Unit`. Hashes change; that is fine (migration cost does not count).

What it should do: `Unit` means the one-value data type everywhere in docs and std; the proposition has its own name; a sweep of std/examples/aoc compiles and audits clean. Needs Matt's choice of name.

tickets.title: Postponable lambda kept from its in-place try can settle a shared type before an earlier postponed lambda is checked (argument-order dependence)
tickets.body:
From the SW-846 lane: in apply_args_postponing (check.rs), a postponable lambda that succeeds when tried in place is kept, so it can solve a metavariable (with the unfolded type) before an earlier postponed lambda is checked; the result depends on argument order (alias-functions.md §4). Check whether the remaining argument-order cases mostly come from this.

Investigated 29 Oct (night), no change. With def Counts: Type := List Nat, Counts.size, twice (f: b -> Nat) (g: b -> Nat) (z: b):
- A: twice (c => c.size) (c => List.length c) (Counts.of 1) rejected (misleading E-CANNOT-INFER from the first try);
- B: lambdas swapped, rejected (E-UNKNOWN-FIELD, c: List ?2) with no lambda postponed;
- C: both c.size, accepted; E1/E2: moving z first changes the inferred call type Counts vs List Nat.
Cause: whichever comparison solves b first decides its name; a later Counts never restores it (alias-functions.md place 3). SW-859's mechanism is one route into it; the §4/AoC cases are already fixed (SW-846) or not this mechanism.
Rules tried with a temporary switch: R1 (after one postponement, postpone all later postponable lambdas) accepts A, E2 but newly rejects examples/accept/lambda-postponed-alias.sw and a record-literal case; R2 (postpone all) accepts A, B, E2 but rejects lambda-postponed-alias.sw and twice (c => Int.abs c) (c => c) 3.
Options for Matt (lane's D1565/D1566): (a) leave, document with place 3; (b) R1; (c) R2; (d) retry with R1 then R2 only when the whole call fails (untested); and fold into a place-3 design (SW-858) where a later unification can restore the alias name. Lane recs: (d) if wanted before place 3, else (a); yes to folding into place 3. Repro files were in the session scratchpad (o/A.sw-F.sw).

tickets.title: Literature research: lessons (how NOT to run it) and where the partial results are; PAUSED
tickets.body:
PAUSED (Matt, 29 Oct 2026). Literature trawl SW-894 went badly. This ticket records how NOT to run it, and where the partial results are. Restart only on Matt's say-so.

== What went wrong (don't repeat) ==
1. Lanes couldn't read papers and nobody checked first. No PDF tool is installed (pdftotext, mutool, qpdf absent) and WebFetch can't read PDFs. Elaboration, proof automation and kernel registers were written largely from abstracts. Fix that works (tested): `nix shell nixpkgs#poppler-utils -c pdftotext paper.pdf -` (package name has a hyphen; `poppler_utils` is the old name and fails). Test the toolchain on a real paper BEFORE starting a lane.
2. Caveats were buried. Each lane listed "sources not reached / abstract only" at the END of its report; the orchestrator relayed the findings and rankings and dropped the caveat. Rule: every register and every report must START with counts: screened / carded / read in full / not read. Every card says "Full text: read (source)" or "NOT READ"; NOT READ supports no ranking or recommendation.
3. Unverified claims were relayed as fact. Lanes said "the session's web-search budget ran out"; the orchestrator first repeated it, then (after one successful search) wrongly said there was no budget, without checking the docs. The docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, "Session search limit"): an interactive session has 200 WebSearch calls shared with ALL subagents; at the limit searches silently do nothing; refills ~100/hour (v2.1.290+, CLAUDE_CODE_WEB_SEARCH_REFILLS_PER_HOUR); cap raisable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION; /clear resets. Seven parallel research lanes at ~30-40 searches each exhaust it. Plan the search budget; run at most one searching lane; lanes report immediately if searches start doing nothing.
4. Too many lanes at once (up to 4, plus helpers). Stopping a lane does NOT stop the reading helpers it spawned; they kept running and reporting after "stop". After stopping a lane, check ListAgents and stop its children.
5. Decision spam: each lane asked 2-3 decisions; the orchestrator listed them all. Keep to one or two decisions at a time.
6. Personal data: the orchestrator once sent Matt's email address to the Unpaywall API (one request, DOI 10.1145/3434341). Never send personal data to any service. Use Semantic Scholar's API (no email needed) for open-access lookups.
7. Leads can be wrong: the kernel redo's readers found the first kernel register misstated papers (Géran says nothing about Lean's level normaliser; the sort-polymorphism paper doesn't use "quality variables" and mechanises nothing; the definitional-inversion paper isn't about Lean with quotients; MetaCoq found one Coq kernel incompleteness, not a soundness bug). Re-derive claims from full texts, never from a previous register.
8. Access problems that remain: ACM DL returns 403 / HTML to scripts; HAL sometimes returns a bot page (check `file x.pdf`); TU Delft repository refused connections; image-only PDFs/slides can't be read (no OCR). Keep a "for Matt to fetch" table.

== Process to use next time ==
Before starting: test pdftotext on a real paper, check the WebSearch budget headroom, give the lane a reserved D-number range and the reading protocol (counts first, read in full or NOT READ, for-Matt-to-fetch table, no personal data). When it reports: verify its counts and a sample of cards against the files before relaying; lead with how much was read. Log progress as you go. Merge only after reading the diff and running the merge tier.

== Partial results and where they are ==
On main, docs/research/ (index README.md):
- inductives.md: RELIABLE. Screened 56, carded 21, read in full 19, not read 2 (counts line checked; cards state how read).
- infrastructure.md: RELIABLE for what it read (59/26/24/2), but its searching stopped when the shared search pool ran out; §9 lists what wasn't searched.
- kernel.md: UNRELIABLE (deep reads rest on abstracts; several claims shown wrong, see 7).
- elaboration.md: UNRELIABLE (many cards from abstracts).
- proof-automation.md: UNRELIABLE (most cards from abstracts).
- effects.md: UNVERIFIED (lane says it extracted PDF text itself; how much it really read is unknown).
Not merged:

tickets.title: Consider congruence closure in cases (D2000): first show it would simplify existing proofs
tickets.body:
From the proof-automation research register (docs/research/proof-automation.md §5.1, ticket T1, decision D2000), redone from full texts 30 Oct 2026.

Idea: a congruence-closure step inside `cases`, as in Lean 4's `grind` and every SMT solver, using only the facts already in scope. Equations in scope are grouped into classes of equal terms, closed under "equal arguments give equal results". Two different constructors in one class makes the branch impossible; both sides of the goal in one class proves it. Stage 2 would apply each local ∀ hypothesis once to the matching facts. Probes that fail on main today (register §5.1): (1) `xs = Cons 1 Nil` and `xs = Nil` both in scope; (2) `f a = c` from `a = b` and `f b = c`; (3) `(y: Nat) → lookup = Some y → y < 5` with `lookup = Some y0`, goal `y0 < 5`.

Assumptions of D2000 in full: (A1) comparing class members by their computed form, as `cases` compares atoms now, is enough, without full conversion inside the closure; (A2) the classes at one `cases` node are small (tens of terms), so the step costs little when it fails; (A3) congruence steps written with `J`, with `Bool.uniqueEq` or `DecEq.uniqueEq` equating proof arguments, type-check for the dependent calls the target proofs contain.

D2000 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): NOT prioritised yet. First gather evidence that it would simplify EXISTING proofs. Before any design: survey std, examples, aoc and games/rogue proofs for steps that chain equations by hand (Eq.trans/Eq.sym/Eq.cong chains, rewrite sequences, matches that only exist to rule out a constructor clash, manual instantiation of a ∀ hypothesis) and that a congruence-closure step in `cases` would make unnecessary; count them, list file:line, and rewrite a few by hand-simulating the step to show the saving. Also cross-check against the cases follow-ups in SW-608. Prioritise only if the survey shows real savings.
30 Oct (survey lane): rebased, read §5.1/D2000, cases.rs closers, proving-guide; starting grep survey of std/examples/aoc/rogue.
30 Oct (survey lane): probes on main: cases fails p2 (even x = True, even x = False ⊢ Void), p3 (o = Some 3, o = None, Option var), p4/p8 injectivity via shared term, p6/p9/p11/p12/p14; passes Nat trans (omega) and h ⊢ h. Writing a leaf classifier for Eq.trans/sym/cong chains next.
30 Oct (survey lane): trial edits (reverted) replacing steps by today's cases: 8 already close (Day06 x5, Day24 settleMore, rogue Loop:24, Rules:24); 12 fail today (Day06 stepTurns, Day16 Moves x3, Day13 Cramer, rogue Loop:20, Day15 sameBox x2, Day17 comboUnique, Day23 x3). Hand-simulating CC on the failures next.
30 Oct (survey lane): 32 sites tried in situ (reverted): 16 already close with today's cases, 16 fail; hand-simulated CC closes 14 of the 16 (3 only with disequality, 1 only with stage 2), 2 unclear. Line savings ~0 per site. Writing docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md.

EVIDENCE (30 Oct, branch worktree-agent-a1fb65a24d4a7ede6, 99e85ba2, docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md): Congruence closure would close steps today's cases can't, but it saves almost no lines. Candidates (multi-step, all-local leaves; lenient classifier): (a) Eq chains 64 + 11 with And projections; (b) rewrite <locals> in rfl/<local>/at 88/22/19; (c) clash from 2+ local equations 63 (39 are one std Map/Set/Ord shape); (d) local ∀ instantiated 14; (e) helper lemmas 1 (rogue someNotNone, which today's cases already does). 32 sites tried in place (reverted): 16 already close with today's cases, 16 fail. Hand simulation of the 16: 6 close by stage 1 at the root, 4 at the first open case only, 3 only with disequalities, 1 only with stage 2, 2 unclear. Estimate: about 150 sites, about 0 lines each (each step becomes `cases` on the same line, about 30 chars); 4 lines saved in 21 sampled cases; about 10-30 lines across about 70k proof lines. Separately, 389 one-hypothesis clash arms are already closable by today's cases and were never converted. The friction notes have no complaint about chaining local equations; their Eq.trans uses are workarounds through library lemmas, which CC over local facts doesn't reach. Recommendation: DEFER. The evidence that sites exist is moderate (hand simulation, not an implementation). The evidence that line savings are negligible is strong. There is no evidence either way on ease of writing.

D2060 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): DEFERRED to backlog. Evidence: docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md. If revisited, start with the narrower check: two local hypotheses `t = C1` and `t = C2` about the same term with different constructors close the branch (39 of about 75 chain sites), not full congruence closure.

tickets.title: Error enumeration for soundness testing (D2031): one type mismatch at every check site, kernel first
tickets.body:
D2031 (infrastructure register C3, §5.1 "Error enumeration", T2), from the Eris paper (Sotiropoulos and Su, PLDI 2026, doi 10.1145/3808320, read in full). Matt, 30 Oct 2026: backlog for now.

Idea: from an accepted program, at every place the checker compares an expression with a known expected type, substitute one expression of an incompatible type (one change per variant); every variant is ill-typed by construction, so any acceptance is a soundness lead. Stage K (kernel, small): over kernel terms, at the check sites in crates/core/src/check.rs (arguments, ascriptions, constructor fields, let values, case branches, definition bodies); oracle: refused with E-TYPE-MISMATCH / E-UNIVERSE / E-REFL; out-of-budget variants dropped. Stage E (elaborator, tooling): source-level, using the hover record of expected types; coercions, postponed comparisons and numeral defaults count as compatible. Options: (a) random overwrites in the existing 400-case daily fuzz run; (b) error enumeration, kernel first, on demand (task fuzz:enum) with a small daily sample. Recommendation: (b), stage K first. Assumptions in full: infrastructure.md §8, D2031.

tickets.title: match last resort: generalise at the end and re-check when only the match's own alternatives fix an unknown (step 4.0 follow-up)
tickets.body:
From SW-817 step 4.0 (D2095, 31 Oct 2026): a generalising match now waits while what it reads holds an unknown. If the only thing that would fix that unknown is the waiting match's own alternatives, it waits for ever and the program is rejected, e.g.
  let g := acc => match List.length [acc] with | Zero => 0 | Succ k => plus acc k
  n   -- g never applied
Main accepted this before step 4.0. Fix as Lean does as a last resort: at the end, generalise anyway, then re-check the choices (occurrence test, motive) once the alternatives have solved the unknown. See postponement.md "As built (step 4.0)". No corpus program has this shape.

tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 12 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026).
(1) `match e:` inside a `decreasing` definition is lifted to an unnamed function taking `rfl`; matching on the same call in a proof gives E-MATCH-MOTIVE ("`rfl` can't prove this") and the suggested fix (helper with a written signature) can't be followed since the lifted match has no name. (2) BUG: a lambda in a recursive call's argument, inside sumBy's callback, becomes an unknown `x` in the termination goal (`⊢ List.length x < List.length xs`); a let is as opaque. Lane has a 3-line repro (in NOTES-2021 day 12). Workaround: top-level helper. Fix: keep the argument in the goal (medium).
(3) Couldn't prove counting search = length of listing search: `List.sumByCong (next cave) _ _ (…)` left both function args as holes; writing the lambda out makes a different lifted match. Workaround: list then count (2.0 s vs 1.3 s). Fix: infer a congruence lemma's function args from the expected type first (near SW-963 item 2) (medium).
(4) `decreasing` takes at most two parts; needed three (small).
(5) After `match e:`, [GOAL] showed the goal unrefined while rewrite at the same spot reported it refined. Printed goals capture variables: `List.Any (y => y = y) …`; search --at printed `(c => c == c)` (small each; capture is a printer correctness bug).
(6) No generated constructor injectivity/disjointness lemmas (also SW-963) (medium).
(7) `search '(?b: Bool) ≠ True → ?b = False'` doesn't find Bool.falseOfNotTrue; conclusion-only pattern lists it third. Cause unknown (small-medium).
(8) audit warns on every theorem about a successful parse (random texts never parse). Fix: counterexample search tries the namespace's test inputs (small-medium).
(9) Minor inference: List.distinctNil after rewrite needed [a := Text]; let-bound lambda has no expected type so rewrite inside fails; depth argument hole not inferred (small).
Cross-day/cross-year imports now carry shared lemmas: day 12 imports 2024 day 24's filterNoLonger and 2021 day 10's toNatAtMostOne.

tickets.title: Day 13: search --at fails after constructor match (context order); cases arg solves holes before expected type; foldRight not structural; x✝ name clashes
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 13 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026).
(1) search --at refuses goals after a match on a constructor with fields: `E-SEARCH-AT … unknown name 'line'`. The goal context lists a refined hypothesis before the pattern variable it mentions (`h: line < 3` above `line: Nat`); equation-style inductions do the same. 13-line repro in NOTES-2021 day 13. No workaround. Fix: order the context by dependency in the goal display and in search (small-medium). High value: it blocks search --at on most proofs after a match.
(2) A `cases` argument solved its call's holes before the expected type: `P.ext _ _ cases cases` said "expected `q = shift b p`, but this has type `q = q`". 6-line repro in notes. Workaround: write the values. Fix: unify result with expected type before checking proof arguments (medium; same family as SW-963 (2), SW-967 (3)).
(3) List.foldRight doesn't compute on Cons (it's foldLeft over the reverse), so omega can't use it. Workaround: lemmas from List.foldRightCons. Fix: note at foldRight or a structural definition (small).
(4) Search pattern `P → _` seems to match P only as the first premise: `List.find _ _ = None → _` missed List.findNoneNotMem (small).
(5) cases prints two different variables both as x✝/y✝ (`spot = { x = x✝, … }, dot = { x = x✝, … }`). Fix: number them (small).
(6) Definitions/theorems whose result is a defined function type need a pattern for the hidden argument; the message explains it well; worth a doc line (small).
(7) New evidence for SW-967 (8): audit also warns when a hypothesis is membership in a function's output.
Seen again: no eta for records (SW-960 (4)).
Std candidates: List.get of map over List.range (Some below n, None past it); List.get (List.range n) i; members below the list maximum.

Triage, 15 Nov (Sonnet, SW-2015):
- DONE: (1) search --at after a constructor match (context order): SW-989 (stop --at refusals) and SW-1000; (5) cases printing x✝ for two variables: SW-1000; (2) cases argument solving holes before the expected type: postponement fixes it (postponement.md:3295, 3319). All three retested in SW-3429.
- COVERED: (4) search pattern P → _ matching P only as the first premise: SW-2186; (6) documentation line for a defined function type result: not filed (small; guide pass). 
- Not filed: (3) List.foldRight not computing on Cons is by design (foldLeft over the reverse); std has List.foldRightCons and SW-2851 adds foldRight lemmas.

tickets.title: Day 15: Map/Set slow in interpreter (heap PQ for Dijkstra); hoisting field reads 2x speed; counterexample search skips records with functions; rewrite fn-equation hidden diff; division needs nonzero proof
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 15 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026). Run: 17.6 s interpreted (20.3 s --no-cache; ~50 s in the loaded merge tier, now daily-only), 4.5 s --native, 2.9 s --js.
(1) Std Map/Set are slow in the interpreter: 250,000 ordered inserts into Map Nat Nat ~1.7 s, ~3.8 s with Position keys; most of part 2's search time. Building every edge 1.6 s. Fix: heap-based priority queue for Graph.distances (medium); runtime-backed maps (large).
(2) A field read inside a lambda is recomputed every call: `position.row % cave.height` recomputed rows.length 4x per call; 31.7 s -> 17.6 s by hoisting `let height := cave.height`. Nothing warns. Fix: performance doc line (small); lift such reads when compiling (medium).
(3) Counterexample search skips the main theorems: "no inputs for `risks`" (record with a function field) and "nothing decides" Rectangle (∀ over list members). Fix: decide that ∀ as xs.all (small-medium); generate function fields from finite tables (medium).
(4) rewrite with an equation between functions fails with a hidden difference: `rewrite same in …` (same: levelAt cave = cave.risks.levelAt) E-TYPE-MISMATCH with both sides printed the same (difference inside …); `rewrite <- height` likewise; J with explicit motive works. Cause speculative. Fix: print the first differing subterm (small-medium).
(5) / and % need a nonzero-divisor proof: nested `if tall: … if wide:` in program and spec, Nat.decEq matches in proofs. Fix: total division as in Lean, or variants (design question; ties to division track).
(6) Messages: Bool.andLeft _ _ rest2 on a refined rest2 gave E-UNSOLVED without the helpful "already refined" note (small). A goal printed a Map's internal tree over thousands of characters (small). Errors printed twice when a namespace failed to load (small).
(7) search --at couldn't see Graph.distancesShortest closes the minimality goal because the conclusion is a defined Prop of two conjuncts; fix: index each conjunct (medium). Plain search missed Nat.divLeOfLtMul (stated with Succ b * d, ≤ b).
Std candidates: Graph.distancesReach (small); grid module: day 15 imports day 9's Position just for its lemmas (medium; SW-960, SW-965).

tickets.title: Day 16: bitsOf check time doubles per bit; rewrite of x/2 rewrites inside x%2; catch-all arm learns nothing; search --at fails on ✝ names
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 16 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026). The cases panic is its own ticket (see below in the board).
(1) Checking `bitsOf w n` on an unknown n doubles in time per bit: 8-line repro in NOTES (0.15 s at 9 bits, 0.63 s at 15, 10.1 s at 19). Guess, unverified: nested / 2 and % 2 copy the term. Day 16 proofs take 14 s cold because of it. Workaround: state each step over variables (medium).
(2) rewrite ran out of budget comparing a term with itself (fields vs fields), a side effect of (1). Fix: syntactic comparison first (small).
(3) E-RESOURCE "a value was too large to show … Eq.trans" with no location where a type mismatch belonged: `_` arguments inferred from an already-computed expected type. Same family as SW-963 (2), SW-969 (2), SW-971 (1) (medium).
(4) rewrite of `x / 2` also rewrote inside `x % 2` (which computes to x - x / 2 * 2). Workaround: rewrite % first. Docs line (small).
(5) In `match n with | 0 … | 7 … | _`, the `_` arm learns nothing about n; omega found the model n = 5. Workaround: Succ×8 pattern. Fix: give the catch-all arm the facts n ≠ 0 … n ≠ 7 (small-medium).
(6) Decreasing through an earlier recursive call's result isn't possible; run-time length guards stand in. Docs example (small); results carrying their decrease (large).
(7) Goals list every superseded `read✝` after each match (small).
(8) search --at: refused a goal after a `_` pattern ("E-PARSE: unexpected character `✝`", new, small); refused another "unknown name `group`" (SW-967 (5)); didn't offer a hypothesis as a rewrite (small-medium). ~14 s per query from re-checking the slow namespace.
New evidence SW-960 (3): Bool `a > b` on Nat isn't Nat.decLessThan.
Proof found a real decoder bug (a total-length operator whose length ran past the transmission was accepted; all tests passed).
Std candidates: fixed-width Nat.toBits with round-trip lemmas; takeAppend/dropAppend with a length hypothesis; Some (a, b) injectivity; List.maximum lemmas (imported day 14's maximumSome; SW-971 (7)).

Triage, 15 Nov (Sonnet, SW-2015):

tickets.title: Kernel: refine context types lazily at case splits (case cost O(cases x context) today; lifts SW-1053's 64-hypothesis cap); also count Int/char literal hypotheses toward the cap
tickets.body:
From SW-1053 (2 Nov 2026). The kernel refines the whole context at every case: check_num_case (crates/core/src/check.rs:1195 on 4 Nov, its `refined` closure at :1249-1254) runs substitute_in over the whole environment and every context type — a read-back and re-evaluation per entry — at each number; check_case (begins at :853) does the same per constructor. So a case split with many hypotheses in scope costs O(cases x context). This is why a catch-all equation after N number arms costs N^2 (SW-1053 capped it at 64).

Idea: record the pending substitution per branch (variable, value, environment) and apply it to an entry's type only when it is looked up (variable type lookup ~line 243; the matched variable's type ~870, ~1215; nested case refinement and the index unifier apply what's pending first). Entries that are just their own variable can be skipped outright (cheap and safe on its own). Effect: each arm of an equation proof touches only its hypothesis and the goal, so the cap could be lifted.

Cost/risk: trusted kernel. Must stay equivalent to eager refinement (eval(quote_folded(v)) gives the same value), keep checked terms and hashes (Term::Eq's filled-in type is read back from these types), and compose nested refinements in order. Skipping entries that don't mention the variable doesn't help here (every hypothesis mentions it).

Also from SW-1053: the 64 cap counts only Nat hypotheses — Int literal hypotheses aren't counted, and a big character table's merged notListed is one hypothesis with the same N^2 proof cost. Cover those with the cap (small) unless this kernel change lands first.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: SW-1106 (done, 20f98102d 'a branch's refinement returns values that don't mention the matched variable as they are') already removed part of the cost. What remains: the per-entry read-back and re-evaluation for entries whose type does mention the variable; re-measure before building.

tickets.body:
Step 1 result (Sonnet, 2 Nov 2026; under load 7-37, re-time before citing). SW-861's natural form is fused on the machine now (01462c09): Std.Parse Parse.next over 160,000 chars, natural vs pair form same user time (~4.6-4.8 s vs 4.55-4.64 s), natural 13% less memory (1.39 vs 1.60 GB); the 28 Oct 9.4 s / 2.2 s doesn't reproduce. Discriminator: at 1M operations a fused natural handler completes, an all-non-tail control hits the recursion limit (machine and --js). JS: fuse gets bodies=None so it can't follow a lifted %match; no slowdown seen in --js runs but not confirmed whether those ran on node. Memory grows ~5.8 KB per char in every form (fusion doesn't bound it). SW-738 revert: plausible after a JS check (build --js, big parse in node) and re-running the Parse.runFrom* rfl lemmas. Decline points in fusion.rs (11, each a silent Ok(None) or fallthrough today): partial foldComp; carrier not at the empty row / not state-passing; return clause not Done e; unrecognised handler structure; clause not x,k => ...; k used non-tail at <span>; depth > 200; > 64 matches followed; backend can't see inside match (JS); no arm of a match resumes; no clause resumes. Plus "partly fused" when one clause falls back. Plan: fuse returns Result<Result<Fused, Decline>> with a span; call sites ignore it; `stitchwort check --explain-handlers` calls fuse with the machine's bodies and with None, one line per handler (machine / js / not fused). Scratch: scratchpad/sw-1087/.

tickets.title: Audit vacuity check: false warnings on generated equations; is random search viable?
tickets.body:
From AoC 2020 day 4 (SW-1249, NOTES-2020.md item 6, ranked 2). The audit's vacuity check tries random inputs and warns when none satisfy a theorem's hypotheses. On day 4 all 8-11 warnings were false, all on compiler-generated equations (heightValid.eq.some with hypothesis value.stripSuffix "cm" = Some number; Spec.validValue.eq.if… with (key == "byr") = True): random texts never hit the literals. Same blindness: check --counterexamples missed a deliberately broken height range (between 151 193). tickets.title: Memory runaway: a Fin literal pattern of 2^128 (fuzz case 12893, seed 0x2468) makes check use 11+ GB in 15 s; likely the exhaustiveness check or Fin-literal lowering unfolding the literal into nested FSucc/Succ
tickets.body:
Repro: stitchwort check dev/fuzz-findings/2468-12893.sw (9 lines: the D1079 Fin non-exhaustive example with its 1 pattern mutated to 340282366920938463463374607431768211456). Expected: E-NONEXHAUSTIVE in milliseconds. Actual: >4 GB in seconds on Speedwell, killed at 11.6 GB on Overmind. Found by Overmind job 29 bisecting seed 0x2468's 11.45 GB peak (SW-2418). Check whether SW-2398/SW-2399 (Fin as numbers, 8 Nov) introduced it. Fix: literals must stay numbers through pattern compilation and exhaustiveness (compare against the bound arithmetically); add the repro as a reject example with a memory/time guard. 45 min.

Started 9 Nov 2026 02:27 UTC. Expected: 45 min.

02:37, orchestrator's call: Sonnet's fix (branch lane/SW-2467, b309bc9d3, kept) is a special case (skip the FSucc branch when FZero has no rows and a literal is > 256), adds a bogus W-REDUNDANT, and leaves the class open: a valid `| _, 0 | _, 1000000 | _, _` on Fin (Succ (Succ n)) still passes 4 GB. Not merged (end state). The end state is a numeric lowering of Fin literals in match compilation (compare against the bound arithmetically, as compile_numbers does for Nat), which is core language: Opus (D2506). Cause: compile in crates/elab/src/lib.rs (~line 3700) lowers literal k to FSucc (k-1), building a k-deep tree before checking. Model result: Sonnet, needed rework (partial, special-cased), 10 min (est. 45).

Started on Opus 9 Nov 2026 03:03 UTC. Expected: 90 min. Sonnet's branch renamed keep/SW-2467-sonnet.

03:45, Opus result (branch lane/SW-2467, 1d72a74e1; worktree kept): Fin number columns compiled like Nat (one subtree per written number), FZero/FSucc steps built lazily while checking; small-match kernel terms unchanged, all hashes stable; repro E-NONEXHAUSTIVE in 0.24 s / 110 MB. But a backstop MAX_FIN_PATTERN = 64 with E-MATCH-SIZE refuses e.g. a 256-arm Fin 256 table that checks today (~7 s): a user-visible regression, so NOT merged; held for Matt (morning D question). Decisions it raises: D-a end state for large Fin number patterns (non-refining Fin.toNat lowering vs kernel compact indices); D-b the 64 limit and its wording; D-c missing cases over several columns now print written Fin numbers as numbers (2, False). Root cost: families::enter substitutes through the whole context per FSucc step, ~k^3-k^4 (filed). Elab tests: fin 114, related filters 143, examples+hash 11, test:lane elab 159. Model result: Opus, worked partly (valid huge case refused by the limit), 41 min (est. 90).

Note 9 Nov: SW-2481 merged; a Fin literal up to 256 now checks in under a second (~300 MB), 512 in 3 s / 1.5 GB, 1000 still OOM: the cap could rise from 64 to ~256; the end state for huge literals is still D-a (numeric lowering).


14 Nov 2026 (tidy batch, Matt: "the memory fix ... start that tidy batch"). Orchestrator's call, no D needed: set the cap where main runs out of memory today rather than at 64, so no program that checks today is refused and only an out-of-memory becomes a clean E-MATCH-SIZE. The end state for huge literals (numeric lowering, D-a) stays a later design question. Opus lane: bring the branch up to date with main, set the cap from measurements, merge. Expected: 2 h (Opus).


22:30, Opus lane result (lane/SW-2467: 0985b09cf merge of main, c88fc50d8 cap). Merge: no textual conflicts; semantic ones fixed in the merge commit (main's Leaf::later, Case::pattern, and its free shifted() folded into Tree::shifted; missing::definite looks inside FinNumbers). Measured (Speedwell, load ~10, release, memguard): main is limited by time here, not memory: full Fin K table 128 arms 3.5 s, 256 arms 23 s, 512 arms 174 s / 1.5 GB; one number K on Fin (Succ (Succ n)) 128 2.9 s, 256 19 s, 512 >60 s at 0.14 GB; `| _, 0 | _, 2^128 | _, _` killed at 3 GB in 2.6 s. Lane uncapped costs the same as main. Cap set to 256 (no memory cliff to align with): 257+ is now E-MATCH-SIZE in <1 s; a number 257-~512 that took 20 s-3 min on main is refused (needs orchestrator/Matt OK). Repro E-NONEXHAUSTIVE 0.65 s / 60 MB. Tests: hash_stability 10/10 (fin-pattern-numbers' hashes follow main's std; number vs FZero/FSucc forms hash identically), examples NAME=fin 7/7, elab fin/missing 5, driver elaboration|proofs fin/number_pattern/missing 33. No AoC day uses Fin number patterns.

16 Nov triage: branch lane/SW-2467 has the fix (Fin number patterns compiled as numbers; patterns up to 256, larger refused); 2 days behind main (before the vocabulary sweep). Orchestrator's call: the 256 limit is fine (reversible). Next: a Sonnet lane rebases onto main, reruns its named tests, then merge.

16 Nov 2026 (Sonnet): main merged into the branch (9cbd307d2). Conflicts: crates/elab/src/lib.rs (main's free `shifted` fn and the branch's `Tree::shifted` method: kept the method, gave it main's new Leaf fields texts/unsplit/cases/facts), docs/syntax.md (main's text-pattern paragraph plus the branch's 256 sentence). arm_display.rs (count_cases, set_facts) and mark_text_gaps now walk Tree::FinNumbers subtrees. fin-pattern-numbers.sw `rfl` -> `byComputing`; its two test hashes in the snapshot moved. tickets.title: Intermittent SIGSEGV in the CLI and test binaries under the full tier on Overmind (job 51, 3eda2fa7d): 20 cores, 11 in elab::module::names_and_proofs <- decl_refs <- LibraryIndex::build (OnceLock standard) <- Session::start_in <- host::stack::start, 6 in musl memcpy, 1 in Expr::span, 1 in nav::Index drop. Also wrong results in the same window: 'library file std/Map/Spec.sw doesn't check', rewind mismatches, cache index differences. Passes alone. Suspects: stack overflow on host::stack's MAP_NORESERVE stack (no overflow handler) or pages failing under memory pressure; or a real memory-safety bug
tickets.body:
Overmind job 51, 9 Nov 16:44-17:21, near the 11.6 GB cap. Cores in systemd-coredump on Overmind (PIDs 886309-895875). Failing tests: goal_index x4, guide quotes, named_arguments literals hashes, rewind examples, run_js and run_reference examples, check_cache x2, import_order. Logs on Overmind j51/. Find the fault address vs the stack mapping first. Tricky bug: Opus. 120 min.

Overmind job 52: NOT a stack overflow (sp ~57 KB into a 64 MB host::stack, far from the guard). Two cores: NULL deref at names_and_proofs+1471 (mov (%r15),%rdx), identical pc/sp in two processes. One core: memcpy from an unmapped address while QuickHasher hashes a &str key of HashMap<&str, Vec<Option<module::Receiver>>> in names_and_proofs <- decl_refs <- LibraryIndex::build. So a dangling/corrupt &str or pointer: use-after-free, lifetime or unsafe bug, or a thread race in LibraryIndex::build. Crashing processes were fresh `check --index - <small file> --no-cache`. 9 GB memory pressure alone didn't reproduce it (56 runs); job 51 had load 10-14. Start: read names_and_proofs/decl_refs for unsafe and borrowed &str; ASan; CPU-hog loop. Cores on Overmind j52/.

Overmind job 53: 4552 runs of check --index - --no-cache (import.sw, missing-cases-several.sw), 4 in parallel under stress-ng --cpu 12 (load 15-16), same binary as the cores: 0 crashes. Neither CPU contention nor memory pressure alone reproduces it. Job 51 differed: CLI started by test binaries from temp dirs, std found via the checkout (no STITCHWORT_STD_DIR), many files, near the memguard cap. Next for the lane: ASan build of the full-tier binaries, or reading what names_and_proofs calls for unsafe/shared state.

Overmind job 54 (3c92cf18d, 3 threads, never near the memory cap): one more core, pid 946881, in rewind::emptying_the_caches_changes_nothing_for_the_examples: frame #0 Vec<module::Work>::from_iter over &[ast::Name] with the typed_binds closure <- names_and_proofs <- free_names_of <- nav::Walk::module <- walk_for_navigation <- elaborate_module <- Session::start_in, in a par_map_with_at_most worker thread. So memory pressure is NOT needed; the common point is names_and_proofs (typed_binds). Job 51's crashing tests passed this time.


Lane (Opus, 9 Nov 22:56-23:06, est. 120 min): no bug found in Stitchwort's code; best lead is a Linux kernel bug. The crash path (CLI main -> host::stack::run_on thread -> LibraryIndex::build -> decl_refs -> names_and_proofs) is safe Rust over a freshly parsed, self-owning AST (ast::Name owns its String). The CLI has no other live thread then (main is in pthread_join; the other spawns in elab/core are test-only), and no native code has run yet. The only unsafe code or FFI on the path is host::stack (reviewed: sound, also under musl's TLS-on-supplied-stack), musl and mimalloc v3.3.2 (libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 builds v3 by default).
Lead: Linux 7.0 to 7.1.8 and 7.2-rc1 to rc6 have a bug in page-table reclaim (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM, def_bool y, used on MADV_DONTNEED): zap_pte_range flushes the wrong address when it frees an empty PTE table, so a CPU can keep a stale paging-structure-cache entry to a freed table. Writes get lost, pages read back as zero, pointers go bad, in a single thread too. It's worst on AMD (EFER.TCE) and on Intel with INVPCID and KPTI off. Introduced by 4c640eb4181c (v7.0); fixed by torvalds/linux 478a1c3abebf "mm: fix incorrect flush address in direct page table reclaim" (5 Aug 2026; in v7.2-rc7, v7.2, and stable v7.1.9 and later; v7.0.14 is still unfixed). Ref: BurntSushi/ripgrep#3494, the same symptoms in musl builds. mimalloc v3 purges freed memory with MADV_DONTNEED 1 s after it's freed (prim/unix/prim.c _mi_prim_decommit; purge_delay 1000), and LibraryIndex::build runs just after a second of parsing churn. That fits: no memory pressure needed, Linux only, never on Speedwell (macOS), wrong results as well as crashes.
To confirm on Overmind: uname -r; zcat /proc/config.gz | grep PT_RECLAIM; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/meltdown; lscpu | grep 'Vendor ID'. If the kernel is in the affected range: as a diagnostic, rerun job 51's failing tests with MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=-1 exported (stops mimalloc's MADV_DONTNEED). The fix is a kernel of 7.1.9 or later, 7.2 or later, or the 6.18 LTS (Matt's host config). No code change, no regression test (a kernel bug).

Orchestrator, 23:10: asked Overmind for uname/config/CPU (lane done in 10 min, no code change). Waiting on its answer before going further.

Overmind, 23:12: kernel 6.18.60 (before the 7.0 regression), CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM=y, Intel, PTI on. So the kernel lead is dead. Next (lanes mode, Opus): a Linux ASan build of the CLI and test binaries for job 51's failing set; or that set with mimalloc swapped for the system allocator, to see whether the crashes follow mimalloc. Parked overnight (orchestrator's call): the remaining causes are mimalloc, musl or the compiler, and that needs Overmind time we've given to the night checks.

tickets.title: [Opus] Conversion keeps ~1.6 KB per unfolded level of a decreasing-checked recursion (innerN 2^128: 3.3 GB before the 2M-frame E-RESOURCE); shrink what Unfolding retains, or unfold lazily (fuzz_elab 0x25a5 case 4273)
tickets.body:
Found by Overmind, fuzz_elab CASES=12000 seed 0x25a5, 10 Nov 2026. Input on Overmind: target/fuzz-elab/25a5-4273.sw. Est. 60 min.

Lane notes (Sonnet, 10 Nov 2026): not fixed; cause found, needs a decision or Opus. The check already stops with a clear E-RESOURCE ("recursed more deeply than allowed", 4 s) but only at the evaluator's 2,000,000-frame limit, with 3.3 GB resident. Path: `unify_step` -> `unfold_folded` -> `force_now` -> `value::run`: conversion unfolds `innerN 2^128` (a `decreasing` function, so a fuelled helper) to head normal form before comparing with `innerN 0`'s. Every level pushes a `Frame::Unfolded` (64 bytes) and keeps its `Unfolding` and the helper's per-level values alive: about 1.6 KB per frame (measured: `innerN 200000` succeeds in 3 s and 744 MB, linear in n). A structural recursion of the same shape (no `decreasing`) is cheap (200000 deep: 0.3 s, 147 MB), so the weight is the `decreasing` helper's per-level terms. Not the work limit (10^10 steps, never reached), not postponed problems or a cache, not SW-2467's pattern chain. The options (unlowering `Limits::frames` for elaboration-time conversion only; a bytes-based cap; making conversion unfold lazily one step; shrinking the per-level retention) change what elaboration accepts or touch crates/core, so they are not done here.
Diagnosis (Sonnet lane, 10 Nov): not the step budget; conversion (unify_step -> unfold_folded -> force_now -> value::run) unfolds innerN 2^128 to head normal form, one Frame::Unfolded per level, until the 2M-frame limit gives E-RESOURCE after 4 s and 3.3 GB. ~1.6 KB retained per level (frames are 64 bytes): the unfolding data and the decreasing helper's per-level values. Without decreasing the same recursion costs 147 MB at 200k. Ruled out: postponed problems, caches, SW-2467's chain, SW-2418. Moved to Opus: shrink the retention (crates/core Unfolding) or unfold lazily.

Lane notes (Opus, 10 Nov 2026, stopped early at the orchestrator's restart; no code committed): cause confirmed with a heap profile (malloc_history at 300,000 frames) and a frame census. Two `Frame::Unfolded` per level (`innerN.%go`, `innerN.%step`), so the 2M-frame limit is hit at 1M levels. The frames themselves are small (64 B + a 128 B `Unfolding` each). The bulk (~3 KB/level) is the proof chain: `%go`'s `%rec` passes `Nat.leTrans (Succ y) (m x) k p h`, which holds the previous level's `h`, so every level's proof stays reachable from the innermost environment however the frames go. Each link is a glued `leTrans` call (5-arg spine: Rc 192 B + spill to capacity 8, ~640 B; plus an `Unfolding`) and `p` = `Omega.prove` (6-arg spine, same cost) with its certificate's constructor values rebuilt each level (~880 B, mostly closed terms). Measured (release, --no-cache): 2^128 with decreasing 4.8 s / 3.31 GB; without decreasing 0.83 s / 466 MB (2M levels); 200,000 with decreasing 3.1 s / 744 MB, without 0.32 s / 147 MB. Shrinking alone can't reach the goal: boxing `Unfolding`'s kept value (tried, reverted) saved only 3% (3.22 GB); exact-size spines and sharing closed certificate parts might reach ~2 KB/level at best, against ~470 B needed. Eliding frames for unshared unfoldings would make the loop tail-recursive and run on to the 10^10-step budget with the chain still growing: worse. Lazy proof arguments still chain through environments (~800 B/level est.) and are a large kernel change. So reaching the goal needs either a memory cap on a check (option 3: changes what's accepted, so Matt's call, like the frame limit) or a `decreasing` encoding whose proof doesn't chain (changes hashes; none found). Next: write this up as docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md with a D question (memory cap?), ~30 min. Instrumentation used (pause at a frame count, names of frames, system allocator for malloc_history) was not committed.
Paused 10 Nov for a session restart. Next: write docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md (cause: decreasing proof chain via Nat.leTrans holds every level's h, ~3 KB/level; frames are small) with a D question on a per-check memory cap (Opus, ~30 min). Branch lane/SW-2639 deleted after merge (only the note).

Write-up (Opus, 10 Nov 2026, paper lane, ~10 min): docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md. Found a non-chaining encoding: `f.%go`'s recursive call decides `Nat.leq (Succ (m y)) k` afresh and passes the match's `found` (rfl at run time); the old `h` and `p` appear only in the impossible branch. Kernel and runtimes unchanged, hashes of decreasing defs change. Hand-written model, 200,000 levels with an omega proof: chained 3.0 KB/level (671 MB), fresh check 0.86 KB/level (251 MB), time about the same (measured). Memory cap not recommended (bytes differ native vs wasm). D3474 (number to confirm): adopt the fresh-check encoding? [rec: yes, ordinary Opus lane]. Parked speed findings: argument lists spilled at capacity 8; closed omega certificate values rebuilt per level.
Write-up merged (10 Nov): docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md. Recommends D3474: generated fuel helper decides Nat.leq (Succ (m y)) k afresh at each call (proof rfl), old proofs only in the impossible branch; model 3.0 -> 0.86 KB/level; kernel unchanged; hashes of decreasing defs change. tickets.title: Check cache: a cache directory copied with a project is trusted (its salt travels with it)
tickets.body:
Severity 2 (likely hole, unconfirmed), from SW-2659 (docs/reviews/SW-2659-kernel-soundness-audit.md, F1).

The problem: the salt that should stop 'a cache copied from elsewhere (a committed .stitchwort, a download)' (docs/proposals/check-cache.md §3.1) is read from check/header inside the cache directory (crates/driver/src/check_cache.rs:149-173), so a whole directory that arrives with a project fits. Entries are sealed with plain BLAKE3, no secret. Loaded entries go through admit_trusted_*, which skips type and termination checking. check, test and audit all read the cache by default (crates/cli/src/main.rs:1440-1451, 2690, 2727).

Confirmed: cp -Rp a checked project with its .stitchwort to another folder and check there; the std.* entries keep their modification times, so they were read from the copy, not rebuilt.
Not confirmed: a forged entry proving False (needs the encoder in crates/elab/src/cache/codec.rs).

Fix, one of: (a) seal each entry with a keyed hash whose key is per user and outside any project; (b) audit always checks in full, and check-cache.md says a cache directory is as trusted as the compiler. A trust decision: Matt's.
Also (SW-2672 G3, cache/mod.rs:2671-2688): after a replay, the entry's stated hashes are installed without being computed; later entries' dependency checks trust them. Fix: a mode, on in tests and audit, that recomputes and refuses a mismatch. Part of D3475.

tickets.body:
Review (SW-2868): worse than a missing message: a recursive call in a lifted match's scrutinee is a real recursive call, so the user is told the function doesn't call itself (false) and the induction principle lacks a hypothesis.
SW-2876 lane: make_induct skips with an empty reason (skip("")) when the only recursive calls are in scrutinees; common shape (match f rest with None => …, Some n => Some (n + 1)); readPackets also gets no IH for its scrutinee call. Record a reason at least; giving scrutinee calls hypotheses is a design question. Also consider a debug_assert that no Term::Def(f) call in a generated statement/proof has more than f's parameter count of arguments (catches the SW-2876 class).

tickets.title: f.induct nested splitting follow-ups (SW-2868 review): alt_refute tries only the last equation of a hypothesis (pair scrutinee | (0, 0) | (a, b) skipped); check a catch-all's hypothesis is about the scrutinee and skip guarded alternatives with their own reason; lift the type-parameter skip by stating the helper at the instance generalised over its free variables ({a} (y: Option (Option a))); test for rows overlapping through Some's field (closed generated, generic skipped). docs/reviews/SW-2868-induct-nested-splits-review.md

Canonical-instance lookup in the unifier: when a method of an unsolved dictionary meets a call to a function exactly one instance uses for that method, pick that instance (Coq canonical structures); no trials, covers instances with parameters (List, Fin n, Set k); replaces SW-2864's unify_guessing_instance. docs/reviews/SW-2864-guessing-instance-review.md (5)

f.induct marks follow-ups (SW-2876 review): debug_assert that unmark(t) == t on a decreasing definition's generated statement and proof before declaring (not a parameter-count check, which fires on function-returning f); run unmark only for decreasing definitions; unmark_step strips only args (or all its fields consistently); make the example show the hypotheses' types. docs/reviews/SW-2876-induct-marks-review.md

A failed rfl on a long chain of stuck sums is very slow to report: the cost is in building the error message (check::refl_error -> Ctx::show), 90M steps / 3.4 s at depth 1,000, over 60 s at 10,000; bound the display. Also: comparing two Nat.add chains recurses on the Rust stack once per level in the per-argument case-tree comparison (E-RESOURCE at depth 1,000 in a test thread). (SW-2875)

The reference evaluator recurses on the Rust stack with no guard when called outside an operation, so deep values in the mode-matrix tests abort the test process (stack overflow) instead of giving E-RESOURCE; seen at depth 300 in proof_equivalence (SW-2875 used a 256 MB thread). Give it the same stack guard as the machine. (SW-2875)

**Progress (lane, 15 Nov 2026, 02:16-03:15).** Done; commit 1b949c461 on `lane/SW-3304`.

- **Cause (traced):** not the review's guess. Written implicits keep a call off `propagation_plan` altogether (the written result mentions them), so with `[t := …]` or `[b := …]` every step goes through `fallback_inferred`: `readsNat` fails in place, the `rest` lambda is held, and `finish_application` compares the step's `Reads (() => bind (?p ()) ?j) ?spec` with the goal by `unify_solving_arguments`. The goal's parser is the outer step's `?j x0`, solved as `bind (nat ()) (x1 => …)`. `same_calls` only fires for two unforced `Value::Call`s, so a call against a *solved unknown* standing for a call of the same definition was unfolded on both sides, through `runFrom`'s handlers, until `?p ()` met `Parse.nat`'s `match` over the state: no solution. With `b` unknown it passed by accident: `?b`, solved at the `value` binder, made the `bind` call stale, `values_differ` re-read both sides, and the re-read put the solution back as a call.
- **Fix:** `unify_step` looks through a solved unknown at either head; two calls of one definition go to `same_calls`. Only while solving from arguments (without that limit day 2 +2.2%, Std.Parse +0.4%). Which arguments wait is unchanged.
- **Numbers** (`STITCHWORT_TIMINGS=decls check --no-cache`, summed per namespace, before -> after; nodes identical everywhere): day 2 proofs 6,890,500 -> 6,896,050 (+0.08%); day 7 6,609,827 -> 6,607,194 (-0.04%); day 18 2,236,096 unchanged; Std.Parse 99,478,662 -> 99,482,727 (+0.004%).

tickets.title: [Opus] Toy formatter: prove the printer correct directly (Matt, 15 Nov 2026: the ambition is no run-time check because the behaviour is proved), so format can drop its re-parse: parse (print t) gives t back for every tree the parser produces, at any width; experiment with a 3 h stop; report what it takes and an estimate for the real formatter
tickets.body:
Matt, 15 Nov 2026, on the goal: "proving the toy printer's correctness directly is a good ambition ... if a program can be parsed, so it's a valid program, then it should be the same program before and after. Formatting for some concept of sameness ... presumably it's going to be the same AST ... idempotence is another key property which I think we want a formatter." So the target theorems: (1) for every program the parser accepts, format's output parses to the same program (the erased tree in the toy); (2) idempotence; no run-time re-parse.

Escalation (Matt, 15 Nov 2026): if Opus gets stuck, rerun on Fable from the lane's branch ("if it gets stuck, we might want to sort of throw Fable at it").

Lane (Opus, 15 Nov 2026, 14:36-15:30, estimate 3 h): branch lane/SW-3418, 8 commits c1b978762..5f8006bb0. Plan and full write-up in tools/toyfmt/NOTES.md, "Proving the printer directly (SW-3418)".

Proved (no goals, no axioms; `stitchwort audit Toy`: 96 theorems, 0 failed, 6 pre-existing warnings; each checked to fail when its rule is broken):
- LayoutProofs.sw: statements and laid-out declarations break at their own column only before else, ) or ] (statementScan, declarationScan).
- CommentProofs.sw: in the rules' documents every trailing comment is followed by a line break before any text, whichever way groups/choices/fills go; a doc ends with a comment waiting exactly when its tree does (exprSuffix, statementSuffix, declarationSuffix).
- ParserProofs.sw: a name token reads back as Var; suffixes stop at a token that isn't ( or . (runsAtomName, runsSuffixesEnd).
- Doc/Proofs.sw: print's 3*size+3 is enough for the printer's steps and for every fits it asks (printBudgetEnough).

Bugs found and fixed, each with a test that fails without the fix: `- -x` printed `--x` (a comment); a comma or bracket after an if's trailing comment went inside the comment; the engine's fits ignored a comment already waiting. The first two were Refused at run time by the re-parse; the third is unreachable from the rules.

Not done: the round-trip theorem itself, so format keeps its re-parse and there's no formatDirect. lexCovers stays as is (proving it is part of the lexing layer, about a day). Left: engine suffix simulation 2-4 d, lexing 2-4 d, reading the layout back 0.5-1 d, parser read-back 4-8 d (gated on a std Parse.operators Runs lemma, 3-6 h), parser-tree WF 2-4 d (or a 0.5 d run-time walk), glue 0.5 d: about 2-4 weeks for the toy; real formatter roughly 2-4 months [estimated, very low confidence].

Part 1 merged (orchestrator, 15:40): proofs of block layout, comment placement (rules' side), engine budget, name read-back; three printer bugs fixed with tests. Main theorem not proved; Opus estimate 2-4 weeks for the toy (low confidence; the toy's estimates ran ~8x high). Findings: SW-3439, SW-3440, SW-3441. Next: Fable continues from main (Matt: 'if it gets stuck, we might want to sort of throw Fable at it').

Part 2 (Fable lane, 15 Nov 2026, from 15:29; progress at 16:05): branch lane/SW-3418, commits ecdc5248a..688467403 so far.
- Std.Parse: Parse.runsOperators (completeness of Parse.operators for a precedence-shaped operator tree), runsRecursiveWith, runsNext, runsLocatedToEnd. operandsFrom/operatorsFrom/locatedToEndFrom's continuations are named functions so lemmas can name them; behaviour unchanged.
- toyfmt D: runsExpression: tokens that spell a well-shaped expression (names, numbers, strings, brackets, fields, negation, operator chains) are read back as it. Lists, calls, if, statements, declarations still to do.
- toyfmt A: the engine breaks a Line/SoftLine after a waiting comment itself (as FillSep did), so the comment guarantee no longer needs a proof about fits; goldens unchanged.
- toyfmt B: lexemeAt's choice is a pure step (lexemeStart) with equations; runsWordLexeme reads a word back.

Part 2 finished (16:20, 50 min of the 3 h; stopped for the model's context, not stuck): 9 commits ecdc5248a..HEAD on lane/SW-3418. Added since the note above: runsExpression now covers lists and calls with their items' comments (every expression but if), with a worked instance (f(a) + b); std Parse.lastReadAfter. 78 theorems (22 std, 56 toy). `task audit:touched -- Toy`: 152 theorems and generated lemmas, 0 failed, the 6 warnings part 1 had; `-- Std.Parse`: 335, 0 failed, 1 old warning (linesBlank). Toy tests 93/93. Not done: if/bodies/blocks/declarations in the parser read-back, the rest of lexing, the engine simulation, rules-to-tokens, what the parser guarantees, formatDirect. Re-estimate: 220-290 lemmas, 3-4 more lanes like this one [estimated]. Decision for Matt: AsWritten declarations keep a re-parse (see NOTES.md). Finding: std_library::the_standard_library_passes_its_own_tests fails at an Args.run test on this branch (not from this lane's changes, by reading; not investigated). Not measured: lexer/parser speed after the added helper calls. Write-up: tools/toyfmt/NOTES.md, "Part 2".

Part 2 (Fable, 50 min) merged: 78 theorems (22 std, 56 toy). Re-estimate: ~220-290 lemmas left for the toy, 3-4 more lanes (days). Open decision for Matt: AsWritten declarations (formatDirect re-parses only files that have one). Findings: SW-3442 (std self-test failing on main), SW-3443.

D3618: every comment gets a place (no AsWritten), in the toy and stitchwort fmt; design in SW-3446.

**Part 6 (Fable, 15 Nov 2026, about 30 min of the clock; commits 3fa646c72, e1b77dad4, 0a407e6d8 and the notes after).** 101 theorems, no open goals or axioms; `audit:touched -- Toy`: 533 theorems, 0 failed, the 10 warnings all on earlier theorems; 98 toy tests pass; no program or std change.
- `Doc/Joins.sw` (59): layer E's adjacency, engine half. `printJoins`/`readingJoins`: through every reading of a document that joins from its edge (`Joins follows`, continuation style over the edges `Plain touching`/`Waiting`), no piece of output is empty and each piece that isn't layout is followed by a line break, nothing, or a piece the document allowed (`Pairs`). A second trailing comment while one waits is refused (`SuffixJoins` is `False` at `Waiting`), and so is an empty one.
- `Syntax/StandProofs.sw` (15): layer B. `Stands`, `standingRun`, `standingLex`: pieces that each stand as one lexeme before the next are `LexemesRun lexemeAt`, so their text lexes to them; `operatorStands`, `definesStands`, `keywordStands`, `signStands`; `minusBeforeMinus` (`-` straight before `-` doesn't stand).

The failing part:

```stitchwort
import Std (Eq, List, Nat, Option, Void)

def next (n: Nat): Option Nat := Some (n + 1)

theorem eachStep ∀ (f: Nat → Option Nat)
    (each: (x: Nat) → (y: Nat) → f x = Some y → x < y) (xs: List Nat)
    (ran: List.map xs f = List.map xs next) (x y: Nat)
    (h: f x = Some y):
    x < y :=
  each x y h

def lambdaFirst (xs: List Nat) (x y: Nat) (h: next x = Some y): Nat :=
  let fact := eachStep _ (a b found => rewrite <- Option.someInjective found in omega) xs rfl x y h
  0
```

`nice -n 19 target/release/stitchwort check FILE` gives `E-OMEGA: omega needs to know the goal ... the goal still has unknowns the compiler hasn't worked out` at the `omega`. Expected: it checks (as it does as a theorem's body, where the after-expected path retries): the lambda's proof search should wait for `_` (`f`), which `rfl` for `ran` fixes later.

Fix direction: rule 2 of the stage 7 design: a failed search (`rewrite`, `cases`, `omega`, `ring`) waits on any unsolved unknown, not only the queue's. Opus (elaborator).

```stitchwort
      + Bool.toNat (x == 4) + Bool.toNat (x == 5) + Bool.toNat (x == 6) + Bool.toNat (x == 7)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 8) = 1 :=
  cases

theorem oneTimerWild ∀ (x: Nat) (bounded: x ≤ 8):
    Bool.toNat (x == 0) + Bool.toNat (x == 1) + Bool.toNat (x == 2) + Bool.toNat (x == 3)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 4) + Bool.toNat (x == 5) + Bool.toNat (x == 6) + Bool.toNat (x == 7)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 8) = 1 :=
  match x with
    | 0 => rfl
    | 1 => rfl
    | 2 => rfl
    | 3 => rfl
    | 4 => rfl
    | 5 => rfl
    | 6 => rfl
    | 7 => rfl
    | 8 => rfl
    | _ => omega
```

- `oneTimerCases`: `E-CASES-BUDGET`, "it split on 9: `(x.decEq 0).holds`, `x.equal 1`, …"; the first open case has `x.equal 3 = True, x.equal 4 = True, …` together (two `Yes` splits that exclude each other). Fix: after a `Yes` split of `x.decEq k` substitute `x = k`, so the later splits compute (or give `cases` the congruence step of SW-904).
- `oneTimerWild`: `E-OMEGA`, "facts: `x ≤ 8` (bounded)", model `x = 0`. The `_` arm's `x ≠ 0 … x ≠ 8` marks (SW-3335) aren't visible to `omega`, as docs/syntax.md says ("the facts aren't hypotheses with names"). A smaller repro: /private/tmp/claude-550/-Users-agent-repos-mdr-stitchwort/8230e28a-2fab-4832-920d-c5160adb7e00/scratchpad/sw3429/item4c.sw (`wildOmega` fails; `wildLet`, which adds `let n0: x ≠ 0 := byDecision` per literal, checks). Fix: have `omega` read the arm's catch-all marks as facts (`x ≠ k`), so the wildcard needs no `Succ`×9 pattern or `byDecision` lets.

tickets.body:
D3618 (Matt, 15 Nov 2026): "I think my initial inclination is actually maybe we should be doing D. Maybe every comment can be placed. Otherwise, we have a sort of kind of partial function for our formatter where we can format almost everything except if you happen to have a comment in a weird place, in which case it gives up for part of the file. So maybe both in Stitchwork and in our toy language, we should support this."

Progress (Opus paper lane, 15 Nov 2026, 16:41-16:55): design note docs/proposals/every-comment-placed.md (uncommitted, in the main checkout). Measured: 0 of 43,404 declarations in the repo are left as written (by construction: S40's count test); probes of awkward positions: stitchwort fmt keeps 11 of 24 (7 "comments": a trailing comment drifts past code the rules put on its line; 4 "comment no rule places": LineStart breaks at the statement's column or 0), the toy keeps 17 of 20 (no tree slot for comments on =, then, operators, brackets...). Principle: a comment stays next to its token (own-line above the next token, trailing after the previous one), and the printer adds a "comment break" wherever the layout doesn't already break, indented as a continuation (floor: 2 deeper than the broken line); one special case (own-line comments before a closer indent like the items). Toy: Trivia on every token, AsWritten and the comment count go, format never re-parses. Plan: lane T (toy, Opus, est. 3 h, after SW-3418 part 3 merges), lane R (stitchwort fmt engine, Opus, est. 2 h, can start now). Question: D3619 (adopt the principle with its rare odd layouts) [rec: yes].

D3619 (Matt, 15 Nov 2026): yes to formatting code with a comment anywhere, and the layout needn't be beautiful: "if you put comments in weird places, then weird things will happen, and that's justifiable. And if we discover that people are putting comments in weird places for good reasons, we can improve the formatting on a case by case basis". He was unsure about the token-ownership rule ("Maybe it's fine, but I don't really know"): not approved as such; the orchestrator treats it as an implementation choice, judged by the requirements (never give up; the comment stays beside the code it was next to; formatting twice changes nothing), and will show Matt real before/after output from the lanes.

Second layout-changes-the-parse case (Overmind, seed 0x956 case 244012, 'input has ], where the output has Alt {'): fmtbugs/arms.sw — a match whose arms sit at inconsistent columns (15 then 6) after a one-line header; the formatter's re-indent regroups the arms. Decide the right parse for both cases; both caught by the tree check, nothing written.

Third case (Overmind, seed 0x959 case 93278, 'input has ty: Seq( where output has ty: App('): fmtbugs/seqtype.sw — def names: / List / Text := … : a type split over lines parses as a sequence; the formatter joins it into an application. All three cases: the parser treats continuation lines in a type or match position as layout structure. Decide the parser's rule for continuation lines once, then make the formatter agree (or refuse).

Lane (Opus, 16 Nov, est. 60 min, ~25 min): one parse per case decided.
- row.sw: the parser was wrong. After an arrow ending its line, a `{e}` line at the block's own column continued the line (as docs say) but `peek` hid the `{` as a stop, so `result_type` missed the row and read `{e} a` as a record applied to `a`. Fixed in `Parser::result_type`; parser test a_row_on_the_line_after_its_arrow_is_a_row.
- arms.sw: the parser was right (match alternatives at 15, a `|` at 6 is the definition's arm). The formatter put the header match's one alternative on the header line (S20), so the arm below joined it. Fixed: the header is printed as inside an arm when arms follow, so the match's alternatives go on their own lines at 8; fmt test a_match_in_a_header_with_arms_after_it_keeps_its_alternatives_below; S20 in formatter-style.md says so.
- seqtype.sw: the parser follows the documented rule (an expression starting on a new line is a block, so `List`/`Text` at one column are two statements). The formatter joined a block type to the `:` when there are no parameters. Fixed: a block type starts below the `:`; fmt test a_result_type_that_is_a_block_starts_below_its_colon.
- D candidate (not implemented): a type is never a block. A `let`'s type and a `match` scrutinee already read lines at one column as one expression (expr_inline); a definition's result type and a parameter's type read them as a block, so `def names:\n  List\n  Text` is `List; Text`. Rec: read every type after `:` as one expression, as `let` does.
